source_name: Dan slovenskih bančnikov / Slovenian Bankers' Day (ZBS flagship annual event)
why_relevant: The flagship annual gathering of Slovenian banking leadership, traditionally at Brdo pri Kranju, with keynotes by the ZBS director, supervisory board president and Bank of Slovenia figures. Speeches are the most candid public statements of sector strategy and are dated and archived.

source_name: ZBS – Sporočila za javnost in novice (press releases & post-event write-ups)
why_relevant: Where ZBS publishes post-conference summaries naming speakers and conclusions — e.g. the June 2026 banking conference 'Ko se svet lomi: Geopolitika, digitalizacija in nova suverenost' and the October 2025 instant-payments press conference on the SEPA Instant regulation and Flik volumes. Frequently the only public record of what was said on stage.

source_name: Bančni vestnik (ZBS journal) – online edition and archive
why_relevant: The only Slovenian banking/finance professional journal (since 1951), published by ZBS. Carries conference proceedings, event announcements, and the English 'special issues' that often reproduce conference papers by bank and central-bank staff. Bibliography pages give per-issue article indexes usable as a structured pointer.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Podelitev nagrad Banke Slovenije (central bank awards ceremony)
why_relevant: Central-bank award ceremony announcements: dated, authoritative, and typically accompanied by a governor's speech. Award recipients and topics signal which research and practitioners the regulator considers important.

source_name: Dnevi slovenske informatike (DSI) – annual conference sites and proceedings (zbornik)
why_relevant: Slovenia's main IT conference (Slovensko društvo INFORMATIKA, Portorož, ~33rd edition in 2026). Bank and processor IT leaders present digital-transformation and core-system projects here; each year has its own persistent site plus a published zbornik (proceedings) — a rare archived record of named IT roadmaps and vendors.

source_name: Slovensko društvo INFORMATIKA – events listing
why_relevant: Organiser hub for DSI and related ICT events; announces calls for papers and partner/sponsor lists, which reveal which technology vendors are courting Slovenian banks.

source_name: Finančna konferenca (Ljubljana Stock Exchange + Časnik Finance)
why_relevant: Largest Slovenian financial/stock-exchange business event (43rd edition, GH Bernardin Portorož). Programme page lists named bank CEOs/CFOs and their session titles — a direct read on investor-relations and strategy messaging. Bridges A1 topics (IR, disclosures) with the events cell.

source_name: Akademija Finance – conference portfolio (incl. Poslovna konferenca Portorož)
why_relevant: Commercial organiser behind many Slovenian finance/business conferences since 1999. Its conference index is a compact pointer to dated events, agendas and speaker rosters across finance, tax and business, several of which feature bankers.

source_name: Delo Poslovni center konference – 'Mobilne tehnologije' conference
why_relevant: Media-house-run conference whose 2026 edition explicitly frames digital payments, blockchain, AI and digital currencies redefining trust and UX. Programme pages name speakers from banks, telcos and payment providers — one of the few Slovenian stages dedicated to retail-payments technology.

source_name: Money Motion (Zagreb) – CEE fintech conference agenda & speakers
why_relevant: The largest regional (CEE/Adriatic) fintech and payments event; Slovenian bank, processor and fintech executives appear as speakers (e.g. Benjamin Jošar, Nina Dremelj, Antonio Argir named in Slovenian coverage of the 2026 edition). Regional stage where Slovenian roadmaps and partnerships are stated in English.

source_name: EBAday (Euro Banking Association / Finextra) – speaker lineups
why_relevant: Europe's main payments-practitioner conference; published speaker lineups (100+ experts, 2026 edition Copenhagen, 16-17 June) are a searchable register in which any Slovenian bank or processor participation surfaces with title and affiliation. Finextra reliably publishes the full list in article form, which is easier to parse than the event site.

source_name: Sibos (Swift) – annual conference programme and delegate/speaker directory
why_relevant: Swift's flagship event; Slovenian banks that are Swift members occasionally speak or exhibit. The programme and session archive is the canonical venue where correspondent-banking and ISO 20022 roadmaps are discussed. Recorded here as a category-level source because the live sibos.com agenda URL was not directly confirmed in this pass.

source_name: WEBSI – Digitalni presežki Slovenije (national digital project awards) shortlists
why_relevant: Slovenia's main digital-project awards (14th edition 2025, record 225 entries; Mastercard Slovenija among winners). Entries are self-declared achievement disclosures by banks, card schemes and their agencies — naming the project, the client, the agency and often the technology. Shortlists reveal digital initiatives never covered in financial reporting.

source_name: Moje finance – 'Naj banka' / najugodnejša banka annual awards
why_relevant: Consumer-finance magazine's methodology-based annual bank rankings (deposits, bank packages, consumer loans). Banks publish the results themselves as achievement disclosures, and the category structure reveals competitive pricing positioning. Award pages on bank sites are dated and durable.

source_name: Bank-side award/recognition pages (e.g. SKB 'Nagrade', OTP banka, NLB media centre)
why_relevant: Each Slovenian bank maintains an awards/recognitions page and issues press releases for wins (e.g. NLB Klik named best mobile and online bank in Slovenia in the independent E-laborat study; OTP/Nova KBM 'best bank in Slovenia'). These are self-declared achievement disclosures with dates, award bodies and often the evaluation criteria — exactly the indirect signal this cell targets.

source_name: Global Finance Magazine – Best Banks / Best Digital Bank awards, CEE & Slovenia
why_relevant: International award programme with an explicit Slovenia country winner each year (OTP banka for 2025). Entries are submitted by the banks themselves, so the accompanying citations summarise self-declared strategy and digital achievements. Structured, dated and comparable year over year.

source_name: Euromoney Awards for Excellence – Slovenia national winners
why_relevant: Country-level award citations based on banks' own submissions; the write-ups typically cite figures, strategic priorities and digital initiatives not otherwise disclosed outside annual reports. Stable per-country URL pattern makes it easy to track annually.

source_name: Davčno-finančna konferenca (DFK) – annual tax & finance conference
why_relevant: 27th edition (Portorož, October 2026). Recurring Slovenian finance-profession conference whose programme regularly includes banking-sector regulation and treasury topics; useful for actor mapping (who speaks, from which institution) even though payments is not its core.

source_name: Bizi.si and Računalniške novice event listings (Slovenian business/ICT event aggregators)
why_relevant: Aggregator listings of Slovenian business and ICT events (e.g. the 43rd Finančna konferenca on bizi.si, DFK on racunalniske-novice.com). Cheap discovery layer for new or one-off banking/payments events that never surface in association calendars.

source_name: GZS (Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Slovenia) – event calendar
why_relevant: GZS co-organises and lists major national conferences (it carries the DSI 2026 listing) and hosts sector associations. Its dated event calendar is a broad pointer to conferences where financial-sector and ICT actors present.

source_name: ZBS YouTube channel – recorded conference sessions
why_relevant: ZBS publishes video recordings of its banking conference sessions (e.g. 'Bančna konferenca, dopoldanski del'). Video is often the ONLY archive of what executives actually said, since slide decks are rarely posted. Transcribable into a durable text record.

source_name: STA / STAkrog – event and conference coverage of banking gatherings
why_relevant: The Slovenian Press Agency reports on Dan slovenskih bančnikov and ZBS conferences, frequently quoting statements from the stage. Where the organiser posts no proceedings, agency and newspaper coverage (STA, Delo, Gorenjski glas, Večer) is the de facto archive.

source_name: Petrol d.d. – Aktualno / obvestila za medije (press room)
why_relevant: Petrol is Slovenia's largest fuel/convenience retailer and an active payments issuer on the acceptance side. Its press room carried the launch of 'Petrol Pay Loyalty' (Sept 2025), described as the first non-bank Visa loyalty payment card in the region, plus EV-charging payment and instalment features via the Petrol GO app. Directly signals merchant-issued card and wallet strategy.

source_name: Petrol d.d. – Petrol klub / plačilna kartica zvestobe product & terms pages
why_relevant: Product and general-terms pages (splošna pravila uporabe) reveal the issuing/processing arrangement, accepted schemes, instalment mechanics and the migration from the old Petrol klub card to Petrol Pay Loyalty. Terms PDFs are the most fact-dense merchant-side payments artefact.

source_name: SPAR Slovenija – Mediji (press room) and customer-services payment pages
why_relevant: SPAR announced it was the first Slovenian retailer to accept Flik instant payments at POS terminals (via NLB Pay), a landmark acceptance-side event for A2A instant payments in Slovenia. Its media page and the dedicated FLIK service page are primary evidence of acceptance rollouts.

source_name: Mercator – Aktualno / Moj M mobile wallet and Pika payment card pages
source_subtype: corporate news + product terms + e-commerce FAQ
why_relevant: Mercator operates the Pika card (a merchant-issued instalment payment card) and the Moj M / M Pay mobile wallet. Its news and general-terms pages document wallet launches, tokenised Pika-in-app payments and accepted payment types in the online store — the deepest merchant-issued credit footprint in Slovenian grocery.

source_name: Pošta Slovenije – Letna poročila (annual reports) and Denarne storitve
why_relevant: Pošta Slovenije is both a large corporate payments user and a retail payment-services outlet (money orders, bill payment, international money transfer). Its audited annual reports carry segment revenue for money services, and it is named in cash-access-network policy debates. State-controlled, so it also publishes 'informacije javnega značaja'.

source_name: Telekom Slovenije – Javne objave (regulated disclosures) and Sporočila za medije
source_subtype: investor relations / regulated announcements + press room
why_relevant: Listed issuer and a major biller/merchant: carrier billing, prepaid top-ups, mobile-payment partnerships and large recurring-collection volumes. Regulated disclosures plus a media room and a financial calendar make it a reliable, dated feed for corporate-user payment developments.
